title: Towards Modern Topic Models: A Survey of Taxonomies and Paradigm Shifts from Algorithm-Centric to LLM-Centered Topic Analysis
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026
problem: Earlier surveys do not organise the fast-growing LLM-driven topic modelling work.
architecture: Three-way taxonomy: Classical Algorithm-Centric (probabilistic, embedding-based, neural, integrated, special scenarios); LLM-Assisted (data preprocessing, LLM-derived embeddings, post-hoc refinement, evaluation); LLM-Centric (Level 1 prompt-based one-round/two-round; Level 2 agentic and similar systems; interpretation of LLMs as topic models). Discusses expanded task scope, model-level to system-level shift and a roadmap.
key_results: Positions TopicGPT and TopicGen as two-round prompt-based methods and LLooM and SPARK as agentic topic modelling.
Notes that one-round prompting can leave documents unassigned and topics incomplete, and that LLM evaluation can miss domain-specific topics.
strengths: Most recent taxonomy focused on the role of LLMs; resource list maintained online.

limitations.text: Category boundaries rely on subjective judgement; coverage mostly limited to the past three years; may overestimate LLM impact relative to probabilistic foundations.
